solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unhealthy-looking pie

definitions.meaning: a pastry case folded around a savoury filling, as in a Cornish one

explanation.surface: A dodgy-looking pie on the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty describes a pallid face; a pasty is also a folded pastry turnover, a British staple, especially from Cornwall.

clue.text: Person showing off difficult puzzle

definitions.meaning: someone who strikes attitudes to impress others

explanation.surface: A show-off who sets a hard brainteaser.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is both a vain exhibitionist and a baffling question that poses a challenge.

clue.text: Manipulative type lives corruptly around north Georgia

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the next pieces, enclosing them
something corrupted is twisted out of its proper form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A schemer leads a crooked life somewhere in the north of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruptly' shuffles the letters of 'lives', and 'around' makes those shuffled letters wrap NGA, which sits after their third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist in du Maurier's novel Trilby, became a byword for someone who controls another person.

clue.text: Cowardly cry: that hurt!

parts.note: to yell is to cry out loudly
ow is the exclamation of someone in pain

explanation.surface: Someone yelps at a minor pain and is called a coward for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for lacking courage, from the colour long tied to timidity.

clue.text: Lifted floor covering to catch variety of fowl

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the words turns them to read upwards, so they come out backwards

parts.note: a mat lies on the floor
to nab is to catch or seize

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a rug to trap a chicken underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' reverses both pieces together: MATNAB read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken.

clue.text: Welshman embraces large artist

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Dai is the stock Welsh man's name in crosswords, short for David
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Welshman hugs a big painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter famous for melting clocks.

clue.text: Modern-day spiritualist initially notes ecological venture

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: a wager is a bet, a venture of money on an outcome

explanation.surface: A contemporary mystic notes an eco-friendly business project.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Ager follows the alternative, mystical movement of recent decades, a spiritual seeker of the present era.

clue.text: Terribly pleased to obtain a new walkway by the sea?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in, or gain, the following pieces
something done terribly is done badly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to have a fresh seafront promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' shuffles 'pleased', and 'to obtain' has the shuffled letters take in AN after their fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a level promenade, typically along a seafront; the question mark admits it need not be by the sea.

clue.text: One who carries, to shelter, steak

parts.note: a porter carries luggage or loads
to house someone is to give them shelter

explanation.surface: A list of a carrier, a shelter and a steak, read as one bumpy sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Porterhouse is a thick cut of beef steak from the short loin.

clue.text: Reportedly pinch metal

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to pinch is to steal

explanation.surface: A rumour that someone nicked some metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is the alloy of iron and carbon, a familiar metal.

clue.text: In tears, after swilling Greek wine

indicators.note: swilling sloshes liquid around, so these letters are swirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone weeps after knocking back wine in a taverna.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Common weed partly spoilt row, gardener recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the run of letters is read backwards
only part of these words is used, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A weed ruined a garden row, the gardener remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes TROWGAR from inside 'spoilt row, gardener'; 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered plant of fields and verges, toxic to livestock and treated as a weed.

clue.text: Mean to move virtually south, all together

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a different order

parts.note: SSE, the compass point south-south-east, lies only a little off due south, so is 'virtually south'

explanation.surface: Instructions to shift almost due south as one group.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French-derived for in a body, everyone at once.

clue.text: Sailing-ship shifting onshore around cape

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the next piece
these letters shift position into a new arrangement

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A sailing vessel drifts ashore near a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' makes SHOONER from ONSHORE, and 'around' wraps it round C after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts rigged fore and aft.

clue.text: Mentally prepare pup circling outskirts of shady church

indicators.note: one piece goes round, enclosing the others
the outer edges of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A young dog is psyched up while running round a dark church on the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych up is an idiom for getting oneself or another into the right frame of mind before a challenge.

clue.text: Hurries back with a companion, getting vegetable

indicators.note: the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to nip somewhere is to hurry there briefly
CH is short for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone rushes home with a friend to fetch greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Reddish-brown and black vase having gold top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top piece comes first, above the rest

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black
an urn is a large vase

explanation.surface: A colour scheme for a black urn with a gilded rim.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn describes hair of a rich red-brown shade.

clue.text: Graduate, with collection of books on artist, repeated phrase

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible
RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock artist

explanation.surface: A graduate and a library of art books, with a chant on repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or formula chanted over and over in meditation, or a slogan said again and again.

clue.text: Journal regularly ignored Conservative rhetoric

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped, leaving the alternate ones

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A newspaper keeps passing over Tory speechmaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops J, U, N and L, leaving ORA.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, close kin to rhetoric, persuasive speech.

clue.text: Sing, fluctuating rapidly, unknown line after poem

indicators.note: the line comes after the poem

parts.note: y is a mathematical unknown
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A singer warbles an obscure verse after a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switching between chest voice and falsetto, as in Alpine song.

clue.text: Jaguar perhaps bounds half-hidden, pursuing one deer

indicators.note: the following piece chases, so comes after, the one before

parts.note: a Jaguar is a make of car
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: half the word is hidden, so only its first half shows

explanation.surface: A big cat bounds along, half out of sight, chasing a lone deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaguar' suggests the cat, but it is the car maker. 'half-hidden' keeps BOU of BOUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer.

clue.text: Staff with energy travelled by bike

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An employee cycled to work full of beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode is the past tense of ride, used of travelling on a bicycle.

clue.text: Ed put on much weight. And softened?

indicators.note: Ed is put after the weight

parts.note: a ton is a large unit of weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ed gained a lot of weight; did he go soft?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that toned, firm muscles would be the opposite of gaining weight; the question mark flags that toned here means toned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone a colour or sound down is to moderate it, so toned can mean muted or made gentler.

clue.text: Maybe slip beneath English river

parts.note: under means beneath
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing below an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' reads as a stumble but is the petticoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a woman's undergarment, so it is an example of underwear.

clue.text: Suspect pair left for thirty days

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy or not right, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dubious couple were left in custody for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: April is one of the calendar months that have thirty days, as the rhyme says.
